questionText:
Consider the following recurrence relation.

$$T(n) = \begin{cases} T(n/2) + T(2n/5) + 7n & \text{if } n > 0 \\ 1 & \text{if } n = 0 \end{cases}$$

Which one of the following options is correct?
explanation:
Step 1: Analyze the given recurrence relation.
We are given the recurrence relation $T(n) = T(n/2) + T(2n/5) + 7n$ for $n > 0$.

Step 2: Apply the Akra-Bazzi method.
For recurrences of the form $T(n) = \sum a_i T(b_i n) + g(n)$, we have $a_1 = 1, b_1 = 1/2$, $a_2 = 1, b_2 = 2/5$, and $g(n) = 7n$.

Step 3: Find the value of $p$.
Solve for $p$ in $a_1 b_1^p + a_2 b_2^p = 1$:
$(1/2)^p + (2/5)^p = 1$

Testing values for $p$:
For $p = 1$: $(1/2)^1 + (2/5)^1 = 0.5 + 0.4 = 0.9 < 1$.
For $p = 0$: $(1/2)^0 + (2/5)^0 = 1 + 1 = 2 > 1$.
Thus, $p$ lies in the range $0 < p < 1$.

Step 4: Compute $T(n)$.
By the Akra-Bazzi theorem:
$T(n) = \Theta\left(n^p \left(1 + \int_1^n \frac{g(u)}{u^{p+1}} du\right)\right)$

Evaluating the integral:
$\int_1^n \frac{7u}{u^{p+1}} du = 7 \int_1^n u^{-p} du = 7 \left[ \frac{u^{1-p}}{1-p} \right]_1^n = \Theta(n^{1-p})$

Substituting back into the formula:
$T(n) = \Theta(n^p \cdot n^{1-p}) = \Theta(n)$

Therefore, the correct option is (C).
